card.name: Punctuation inside adverse reaction lists
card.fires_on: Commas, percent signs and linking words right after an adverse reaction name or its rate in lists of side effects. It anticipates another listed reaction or a frequency term like common.

modes.label: After percentage
modes.description: The percent sign and comma after a number in a list of reaction rates.

modes.label: After reaction name
modes.description: A comma after a symptom name in a plain list of reported reactions.
modes.example: Gastrointestinal disorders: Nausea<<,>> vomiting, diarrhea, dyspepsia

modes.label: Linking words
modes.description: Words like is, of or and after a reaction name, leading into incidence or frequency wording.
modes.example: and the incidence<< of>> vomiting in the 23 mg group

card.writes: It promotes the word common in several languages, suggesting frequency wording is expected next.
card.plain: It fires at the small breaks in lists of side effects and rates, where the text may say how common something is.
